decisions.rationale: Names one specific inherited thrombocytopenic disorder described as an isolated entity in this family, not a family of diseases.
Thrombocytopenia is a low-platelet condition that covers a family of multiple distinct disorders with different causes, so it is a Disease Class.
'Immunological abnormalities' uses the very general term 'abnormalities', which is excluded and does not name a specific disease.
Duplicate mention of the same specific X-linked recessive thrombocytopenic disorder; the full phrase names one disease and is annotated separately.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §4 (duplicate mentions) and §1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: 'Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome' is a named, specific disease with a single definition.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease) and §5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: 'WAS' is the abbreviation of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome and is annotated as a separate synonymous mention referring to the same disease.
'Immune deficiencies' is a general term; 'deficiency' is explicitly excluded as a very general term and the phrase does not name a specific disease.
Second occurrence of the same specific X-linked recessive thrombocytopenia disease; duplicate mentions within the text are each annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §4 (duplicate mentions) and §1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: 'WAS' in 'classical WAS phenotype' refers to the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome disease phenotype, so it is annotated as a specific disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease) and §6 (synonymous mentions)

decisions.rationale: Here 'WAS' denotes the WAS gene, not a disease; gene or locus names are not disease mentions and are not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate (only disease mentions are annotated; gene names excluded, cf. §5 biological processes)
